question.problem: Given that the random variable $X\sim \textrm{Exp}\left(2\right),$ calculate $P\left(\dfrac 12 < X < 2\right).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda$ has the following probability density function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14129107/assets/e77daa45c1026175eec99e71cb336ad5b8c2a46683170b0f9357a4ad7e9d1bf5.svg)

We're given that

$$
X\sim \textrm{Exp} \left( 2 \right).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14129107/assets/e0b6d1388350fabce97f26601d512e60cfe6ac3ab41230671718ca034c5c3860.svg)Therefore, we can calculate $P\left(\dfrac 12 < X < 2\right)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\frac{1}{2}<X<2) & ={\int }_{1/2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{2}2{e}^{-2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{{e}^{-2x}|}_{1/2}^{2} \\  & =-{e}^{-4}+{e}^{-1} \\  & ≈0.3496\end{aligned}
$$
